product: The Complete System for Mature Women's Skin ($121.07)
avatar_brief: Woman 62-70, in a conservatory or by a window with plants, cup of tea, cardigan. Unhurried. Delivery is specific and undramatic — she gives dates and details rather than adjectives, which is what makes it land as testimony rather than advertising.
hook: Four months. That's how long before I stopped checking whether it was working.
first_frame: Her by a bright window, tea in hand, mid-sentence as if the camera started late. Face fully visible in daylight, no makeup.

beats.vo: Four months. That's how long before I stopped checking whether it was working.
beats.visual: Window light, tea, she is settled and still. No product in frame yet.

beats.vo: I'm not going to show you a before photo. I didn't take one, because I didn't expect anything.
beats.visual: Small shrug, she sets the tea down.

beats.vo: What I noticed was small. I stopped putting powder on at eleven in the morning to fix how my face had gone.
beats.visual: She touches her cheek briefly, matter-of-fact.

beats.vo: It's four steps. Scrub, day balm, eye balm, night balm. Arctic plants. Supports the skin barrier in 7 days, though for me it was longer than that.
beats.visual: The four jars set out on the windowsill in order, sunlight behind them.

beats.vo: A hundred and twenty-one dollars, sixty days or your money back. I'm on my third order.
beats.visual: Back to her face, daylight, no retouching.

beats.vo: The Complete System for Mature Women's Skin. Frøya. Give it longer than you think.
beats.visual: She picks the tea back up. Brand name on screen.

hook: My hairdresser asked what I'd changed. She's done my hair for nine years.
first_frame: Outdoors, handheld selfie, hair visibly just blow-dried, salon window behind her slightly out of focus.

beats.vo: My hairdresser asked what I'd changed. She's done my hair for nine years.
beats.visual: Handheld, outdoors, wind moving the fresh blow-dry. Salon behind.

beats.vo: I said nothing. Then I remembered — I swapped my shampoo about three months ago.

product: Dry and Itchy Balm for Face and Body ($44.00)
avatar_brief: Woman 46-54, sitting on the end of a bed with a laundry basket beside her, dressing gown, late evening. Delivery is quiet and slightly flat — this is the least performed of the three, someone recounting something that mattered without wanting to make a thing of it.
hook: I bought it for me. My daughter's the one who kept stealing it.
first_frame: Her on the end of a bed, laundry basket half-folded beside her, lamp light. A small jar sitting on top of the folded clothes.

beats.vo: I bought it for me. My daughter's the one who kept stealing it.
beats.visual: She picks the jar off the laundry pile, turns it over in her hands.

beats.vo: She's nineteen and her hands crack every winter. Mine's the elbows and shins, same as my mum.
beats.visual: She shows her own forearm briefly, then lets the sleeve fall.

beats.vo: It's chamomile and thistle in beeswax. Soothes dry, itchy skin, supports the skin barrier in 7 days.
beats.visual: Opens the jar, the balm is solid and has to be warmed — she works it between her fingers.

beats.vo: Gentle enough for face and body, which is the only reason two people can share one jar.
beats.visual: Working it into a knuckle, then along the jaw.

beats.vo: Forty-four dollars and I've bought it three times because it keeps leaving this house.
beats.visual: She sets the jar back on the folded laundry, deadpan look to camera.

beats.vo: Dry and Itchy Balm, from Frøya. Buy two if anyone else lives with you.
beats.visual: Lamp light, jar on the laundry. Brand name on screen.
